name: first-round tool-choice expectations v1
purpose: The expected FIRST-ROUND tool for every question eval/tool-choice-probe.mjs asks. Written and committed BEFORE any probe arm ran, so the expectations are not fit to results. Scored mechanically by eval/tool-choice-score.mjs.

labels.recommend_resources: An image-kind / use-case 'which models, LoRAs, add-ons or checkpoints for X' question. Met when recommend_resources is among the first round's calls.
labels.search_models: A named model, an id, a stat, a version, a base model of a named model, or an explicit ranking (most downloaded / most popular / newest / top N). Met when search_models is among the first round's calls.
labels.none: Technique or identity. Met when the first round makes NO tool call; any call is an over-trigger.
labels.either: Genuinely ambiguous: met by either tool. Not used in v1.

extraQuestions.text: what models are best for professional content
extraQuestions.why: The production turn on 0.1.31 that made three search_models calls sorted Most Downloaded and answered with popularity rankings. Lower-case and unpunctuated exactly as the viewer typed it.

notes.T4: 'Why do my generated hands look distorted' is a troubleshooting question the v1 set labels expectTool:false. A recommend_resources call there (e.g. a hand-fixing LoRA) is scored as an over-trigger, deliberately: the set's own label is the pre-registered answer.
notes.L4: 'most downloaded anime models' is an explicit ranking, so search_models, even though it names an image kind.
notes.PROD1: 'best' could be read as a ranking word, but the question asks for fit to a use case, not a popularity order; labelled recommend_resources as the operator's report frames it.
